acceptanceCriteria: Expansion fires only on an exact anchor resolution and is capped; ambiguous anchors produce uncertainty, not expansion.
Each expanded row carries the anchor and the hop reason.
Measured on the frozen retrieval evaluation with no recall regression at fixed byte budgets.
body: Owner requested this on 2026-09-23 after reviewing Tencent/WeKnora (MIT) as prior art; this ticket records an idea, not delivery or promotion. Original Go work only; no source import. WeKnora is an LLM-at-ingest, database-backed RAG platform, so only the mechanism is borrowed and it must stay deterministic, local and read-only under AGENTS.md invariants 4 and 7. Before implementation is called complete, update the owning indexed spec with stable requirements, non-goals, failure modes, acceptance evidence and rollback, and finish normal CEM/OCM, independent review and mandatory gates. Prior art: website-docs/03-features/09-knowledge-graph.md of https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora. GraphRAG there is an LLM entity extraction over the query, fuzzy name match against Neo4j (`n.name CONTAINS nodeText`), one-hop neighbours and relations, and the chunks attached to those entities merged into the candidate set beside vector and keyword hits. The LLM, Neo4j and fuzzy match are out of bounds for Corvint (invariant 7), but the retrieval shape is not. Current state: V1-0084 preserves repository anchors verbatim in lexical queries and V1-0083 proposes an identifier definition/reference graph with budgeted PageRank; neither states the query-time expansion rule. Idea: when a query anchor resolves exactly to a definition, admit that definition plus one hop of its references and its test pair as candidates with the reason `anchor-one-hop`, capped by a small fixed count, before ranking. Exact match only; no fuzzy resolution. Owning spec: docs/specs/task-context-packet-v0.md. Related: V1-0083, V1-0084.
title: context: anchor-resolved one-hop reference expansion as the deterministic GraphRAG rule
